dos.text: Put dependent controls in the slot="nested" slot instead of manually disabling them, MozBaseInputElement's updateNestedElements() sets their parentDisabled from `!this.checked || this.disabled` because moz-checkbox declares static activatedProperty = "checked", so nested elements go disabled whenever the box is unchecked, not only when the checkbox itself is disabled.

donts.text: Don't rely on form.reset() restoring a checked value you assigned with JS after the element connected, defaultChecked is captured exactly once in connectedCallback from the initial checked attribute/property, so later `.checked` assignments change the current value but not what formResetCallback() reverts to.

Don't expect the classic <checkbox> element (toolkit/content/widgets/checkbox.js, which still ships alongside moz-checkbox) to have any interactive behavior, its checked getter/setter only toggles the checked attribute for CSS/image purposes, there's no click handler, keyboard toggling, or form participation built in.
